item.title: [github_trending] DietrichGebert/ponytail
item.description: Ponytail is an npm package (@dietrichgebert/ponytail) that pushes your coding agent toward the persona of the laziest senior dev in the room — the one who says nothing, writes one line, and it works. Its premise is that the best code is code you never wrote, and the README says it works with 20 agents. Useful if your agent tends to over-engineer.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A Juejin post by a developer who switched from Cursor to Codex and has used it for roughly half a month. Cursor, the author says, was his first strong taste of what AI coding can do, while Codex feels less like a coding assistant and more like an autonomous super-agent, closer to the next stage of tooling. Useful for developers weighing which AI coding tool to adopt.

item.description: MiniMax released M3.1 Flash on October 19, claiming it is 88x cheaper than Opus 5.5 while ranking first on both the Agent leaderboard and the Artificial Analysis ranking. The anonymous model Space Bunny, which drew attention on OpenCode and OpenRouter usage charts, was confirmed as an early version of it. The focus is code generation and multi-step task execution at low cost, for developers watching inference budgets.

item.title: [v2ex] [生活] 结婚三年，现在跟我说不生小孩，我该怎么办？求建议
item.description: A V2EX user writes that after two years of dating and three years of marriage, his wife has stayed home without working, spending her days on videos and games, and has now said she doesn't want children. He asks whether her mind can be changed or whether his own expectations are the problem, and says he wants practical solutions rather than judgment.

item.title: [juejin] 面试官问你：“AI 能写 80% 的代码了，公司为什么还需要你？”
item.description: A Juejin post on how 2026 technical interviews differ from two years ago: instead of hand-writing a Promise or explaining React Fiber, interviewers now assume candidates already use AI and ask why a company should still hire them when AI writes 80% of the code. It's aimed at engineers preparing for interviews who need to articulate what AI can't replace.

item.title: [github_trending] cloudflare/security-audit-skill
item.description: cloudflare/security-audit-skill turns a coding agent into a security auditor, orchestrating isolated agents through six phases: reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification and target-neutral reporting. It is the single-repo skill that seeded Cloudflare's fleet-wide vulnerability discovery harness, and it writes independently verified, machine-readable findings to files like findings.json. item.description: Two newly disclosed PHP flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, allow severe remote code execution, and BT Panel has shipped fixes for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 as well as newer branches, so jumping to 8.2 is not required. item.title: [v2ex] [分享创造] den：终极文档维护方案
item.description: den is an open-source project on GitHub (onichandame/den) built on a deliberately simple premise: docs are a project's long-term factual record and just need to be absorbed quickly, so rather than imposing a documentation standard, make everything flat under docs/ semantically searchable. Its author argues existing methodologies all attack the input side, and den attacks the output side. It suits teams whose docs are messy but who don't want to invest in governance.

item.title: [infoq] 北大博士、零一万物联创黄文灏加入字节 Seed 两年后离职，下一步或创业
item.description: Huang Wenhao, co-founder and former VP of algorithms at 01.AI, has left ByteDance's Seed team, according to multiple Chinese media reports; he joined in August 2024 to handle technical project management and planning, later shifted to model evaluation under Wu Yonghui, and may start a company next. A Peking University CS PhD who previously worked at Microsoft Research Asia and BAAI, his exit renews scrutiny of Seed's churn, after reports that nearly 70 technical staff left in a year.

item.title: [v2ex] [生活] 码农幻想：在模型能力上，是否存在这样一个规律，如果某 agent/llm 能让 x%的程序员被取代，意味着能有%y 的教书匠和%z 的医生被取代
item.description: A V2EX poster poses a hypothetical: if an agent or LLM can replace x% of programmers, is there a corresponding share of teachers and doctors it could replace? He then sketches what that ratio might enable — "agent education bases" and "agent pre-diagnosis labs" staffed by local aides and supervised remotely by top teachers and specialists in provincial capitals, aiming at universal access to quality schooling and care. It is a thought experiment only, with no data or implementation plan.

item.title: [github_trending] stablyai/orca
item.description: Orca is an open-source workspace from stablyai for running a fleet of coding agents such as Grok Bot and Claude Code, letting you use your own existing subscription instead of platform credits. It ships desktop apps for macOS, Windows and Linux plus mobile and a remote runtime, under the MIT license. Useful for developers juggling several agents at once.

item.title: [v2ex] [VPS] 问下站内推荐的 digitalocean 的 vps 网络支持国内直连吗
item.description: A V2EX user asks whether DigitalOcean VPS instances are usable over a direct connection from mainland China. He notes the provider was recommended on the forum, but the site looks AI-generated, with pricing for every product pointing to the same VPS selection page and plans starting at $4/month, and asks whether a personal instance could serve as a proxy. The thread contains no answer yet.

item.title: [v2ex] [程序员] 宝塔面板还是挺负责的 凌晨 2 点发布 PHP 更新
item.description: BaoTa panel pushed a PHP update at 2am: versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 track the official releases, while 7.4.34, 8.1.35 and 8.0.27 were patched and packaged by BaoTa itself because PHP only published them on GitHub without a release tarball. Refreshing the software list pulls the updates, and the maintainers recommend running at least PHP 7.4 since older branches no longer receive fixes.

item.title: [github_trending] Graphify-Labs/graphify
item.description: graphify ships as a /graphify skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI, turning a codebase plus its docs, SQL schemas, configs and PDFs into a queryable knowledge graph. Parsing is local and deterministic AST-based, so source code doesn't leave the machine. Worth a look if you want coding agents to answer structural questions about a large repo instead of grepping blindly.

item.title: [infoq] DeepSeek开源最新推理框架：单集群日吞吐155万亿Token，KVCache可保存7天
item.description: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference framework behind its V4.1 Flash online service, reporting 155 trillion tokens per day from a single cluster and roughly $38 per GPU-hour at off-peak pricing. Prefill runs on ordinary 8-GPU servers while Decode uses 64–128 GPU supernodes, with KVCache retained for over 72 hours on both NVIDIA and Huawei Ascend hardware. A companion token codec, deepseek-recipe, ships alongside, though KVCache management and load balancing stay closed.

item.title: [infoq] Anthropic几乎停招初级员工！占比一年半骤降33%：Agent工时已是员工6倍
item.description: Internal numbers from Anthropic show junior staff in its technical org falling from 21% to 14% since early 2025, with juniors dropping from 27% to 9% of new hires. By August 2026 the ratio of agent to human working hours hit 6:1 company-wide and 19:1 in research; engineer code changes rose 5.1x and merge volume 12x in four months, pushing Anthropic to build its own version control system. Managers now commit code nearly twice as often.

item.description: A security advisory warning of critical remote code execution vulnerabilities and urging immediate updates. item.description: A Zhihu question asking which books can be read in China while being banned elsewhere, part reading-list exchange and part discussion of how censorship differs across countries. Only the title is provided here, so the specific books and answers aren't available.

item.title: [infoq] 代码迁移准确率从 5.4% 飙至 97.9%！OpenAI 挑战 COBOL，几十年的老系统真能交给 AI 了？
item.description: On October 19 OpenAI published research on low-resource programming languages. In a COBOL migration benchmark, GPT-6.1 Sol reached 97.9% accuracy at higher reasoning effort, up from 5.4% for GPT-5.6 Sol at low effort; in a separate 20-language test asking models to build a SQLite-compatible database engine from scratch, GPT-6 Astra averaged 87.4% versus 26.8%. The numbers show AI coding closing its gap on COBOL and Fortran, though handing over decades-old systems is another question.

item.title: [infoq] Agent 删库频频发生，几十年前就有的数据库防呆机制不管用了？
item.description: Andy Pavlo, the CMU professor who joined ClickHouse as VP of database research, argues on The MAD Podcast that agent-driven database deletions are an old problem resurfacing — permissions and sandboxing have existed for decades. He also calls vector databases table stakes rather than a moat, puts off-the-shelf text-to-SQL near 60% accuracy, and notes that over 60% of open source databases already carry agent-authored commits.

item.title: [infoq] Cloudflare 开源面向 AI 智能体的决策模型 Clef
item.description: Cloudflare open-sourced Clef, decision models in 9B and 27B multimodal variants that take a state plus a schema of typed questions and return probabilities for every option in one forward pass, with a 64k context and no free-text generation. Clef-Flash, the 9B model, runs at 38.8ms median latency versus 209.3ms for the 27B, and runs on edge GPUs via Workers AI for triage and classification decisions.

item.title: [infoq] 美团企业级 Agent 的平台化应用实践｜QCon上海
item.description: At QCon Shanghai on October 22–24, Meituan R&D director Li Kai will describe how the company moved internal agents from working to trustworthy. Its AgentOS pairs a runtime and harness with skills, MCP, sandboxing, identity registration, permission governance and evaluation, leaving judgment to models and deterministic logic to code, while Multica turns people, agents and business processes into traceable, resumable tasks. The platform serves hundreds of thousands of agent users.

item.title: [infoq] AI 能否取代渗透测试？Cloudflare 的答案是：必须套上测试框架
item.description: Cloudflare placed frontier models inside a Python harness to black-box test its own WAF: the models propose payload variants and review responses, while the harness builds and replays requests and holds the guardrails. Across 45 scenarios the system made 1,107 attempts; 607 formed a filtered set, and human review kept 49 findings, 48 of them command injection or SSRF. The work produced three changes to Cloudflare's managed ruleset, including two new SSRF detection rules.

item.title: [hackernews] eMudhra intermediate CA compromise
item.description: A Mozilla security blog post and Bugzilla bug 2083449 cover a compromise of an intermediate CA run by eMudhra. When an intermediate certificate authority is compromised, every certificate it issued has to be treated as suspect, which bears directly on the public trust chain browsers rely on. The linked pages aren't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available.

It suits creators and developers who want to wire up workflows node by node and run inference on their own hardware. Community entry points include a website plus Discord and Matrix rooms.

item.title: [hackernews] Eight Bits of Trust: eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds
item.description: Scott Helme recovered the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificates straight from their public certificates in under a second, because the keys were tiny integers such as 4, 56 and 115. The compromise was reported to Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla and eMudhra on 17 October; Chrome shipped a CRLSet block that evening and Firefox followed hours later through OneCRL.

It targets web, mobile, and AI developers who want to own their SQL data without assembling a backend from scratch.

item.title: [github_trending] headroomlabs-ai/headroom
item.description: Headroom is a context compression layer that shrinks tool output, logs, files and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM, available as a library, a proxy and an MCP server. The project reports roughly 20% fewer tokens for coding agents and 60-95% for JSON with unchanged answers; its demo compresses a 55,957-token prompt to 24,340 tokens while a critical FATAL line survives byte for byte. Aimed at agent developers paying per token or fighting context limits.

item.title: [juejin] 天天 AI Coding 的你，如果出去面试，你的竞争力是什么？

The author sketches a mock interview for an Android engineer candidate to reason it through. It's aimed at developers preparing to switch jobs or wondering how hiring signals are shifting.

item.title: [github_trending] vllm-project/vllm
item.description: vLLM is an open-source inference and serving engine for large language models, built for high throughput and memory efficiency and originally developed in the Sky Computing Lab at Berkeley. The repo links its arXiv paper, docs site and developer Slack, which makes it a practical starting point for teams weighing a self-hosted LLM serving stack.

item.title: [juejin] 为什么不推荐走Agent开发？
item.description: Writing on Juejin, author Feiyu answers readers' questions about whether to move into Agent development, and his stance in the title is that he doesn't recommend it as a career path. He notes that many training programs push backend engineers toward AI, and argues that long-term growth in Agent work requires certain preconditions — though the excerpt cuts off there. Useful for developers weighing a switch into agent work.

item.title: [github_trending] strelov1/freehire
item.description: freehire is an open-source search engine for IT jobs that claims to pull 3.3M+ live postings directly from company career pages, skipping recruiters, reposts and dead links. It is written in Go under the MIT license, ships a hosted site at freehire.me plus an API, and documents its architecture and sources for anyone building a similar crawler or vertical job search.

item.title: [juejin] 2026年金九银十，我面了22个前端
item.description: A front-end interviewer recaps the 2026 autumn hiring season: with the team expanding, they worked through more than 30 résumés and ran 22 technical interviews, ending with 3 offers and 2 actual hires. Only that opening is available in the source, so the interview questions and candidate assessments that follow aren't included; relevant to developers preparing for front-end interviews or running hiring loops.

item.title: [juejin] 公司从 400 多人缩减到 100 多人，我开始重新思考程序员的未来
item.description: A personal essay on Juejin whose author watched their company shrink from over 400 people to just over 100, and uses that to rethink the future of programmers, touching on the situation of 35-year-old developers and the combined pressure of a weak market and AI. It is not a technical tutorial but one developer's read on an industry in retreat, useful for anyone weighing career plans.

item.title: [juejin] 我用 REA 逆向了付费颜色 APP，结果很意外！
item.description: The post first explains what reverse engineering is and introduces REA, an open-source project that has drawn attention on GitHub, then uses it with AI against a single-player Android game and a learning app. It suits readers who want a hands-on look at where AI-assisted reverse engineering actually lands, rather than a purely conceptual overview.
